entries.title: Interpretation before the bounded pilots
paragraphs: The completed development baseline supports a useful adaptation effect on difficult speech. On the same expanded panel, initial final reduces macro WER from 40.7% to 28.1%. The largest absolute reductions are in AMI and CHiME 6. Common Voice changes only from 8.4% to 8.2%, so the overall gain does not mean equally large benefits for older voices.

Quiet-view WER falls from 59.5% to 41.9%, but substantial errors remain. For initial final, CHiME array-view WER is 79.2% versus 34.0% on worn microphones. Microphone placement and audibility therefore remain important. These descriptive slices do not isolate a causal microphone effect because recordings and repeated source views are related.

All three baseline models produce zero inserted words on the 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes. This is reassuring for those probes only. It does not establish an absence of hallucinations on real background speech, electronics noise or product microphones.

Initial final has the lowest aggregate development WER, while initial best is slightly better on Common Voice. The separate matched panel also contains regressions on some cleaner speech cohorts. Aggregate scores must be read alongside per-dataset results. Frozen-panel findings are documented for context and are not used to choose the next recipe.

The supervisor has automatically moved to the mixed LoRA reference. It will complete the four individual-dataset pilots before considering the single permitted weighting proposal, then compare the one full-tuning pilot. No additional experiment or change in weighting is warranted from the baseline alone.

entries.title: Interpretation of the completed mixed dataset pilot
paragraphs: The mixed LoRA reference completed 10,000 optimizer steps in 39.1 active minutes, stopping at its declared step cap. It visited 69,791 microphone views. Best and final exports are byte-identical, so the scorer reused the same decode and noise probes; their timings are not independent measurements.

On the unchanged 954-view development panel, macro WER is 31.7% versus 40.7% for the W4A8 base. This is a 8.98 percentage point reduction and 22.1% relative improvement. Every dataset improves descriptively relative to that base. These values alone do not establish statistical significance.

The earlier full-duration initial final checkpoint remains better overall at 28.1% macro WER. The short pilot is 3.64 points worse. Duration, exposure and microphone coverage differ, so this comparison cannot establish that expanded microphones are harmful. The mixed pilot supplies the reference for the remaining short-budget experiments.

Quiet-view WER is 48.0%, compared with 59.5% for base and 41.9% for the initial final checkpoint. It produced 0 inserted words on 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes. That small synthetic probe set does not establish behavior with real background voices or the product microphone.

The supervisor has automatically started the Common Voice only pilot. AMI, CHiME 6 and VOiCES pilots follow before the bounded weighting decision. No mixture promotion or method decision is due yet, and no additional trials or hyperparameter changes are introduced.

entries.title: Interpretation of the completed Common Voice only pilot
paragraphs: The age-filtered Common Voice only LoRA pilot completed its 10,000 optimizer-step cap in 34.8 active minutes, visiting 66,314 training views. Best and final exports have the same model hash, so decoding and timings were reused rather than independently measured.

On the unchanged 954-view development panel, macro WER is 36.9%, compared with 40.7% for the W4A8 base and 31.7% for the mixed pilot. The standalone pilot improves every dataset descriptively relative to base, but is 5.23 percentage points worse overall than the mixed reference.

Common Voice WER is 7.75%, versus 8.39% for base and 7.82% for the mixed pilot. The 0.07-point advantage over mixed is small and does not establish a reliable benefit from increasing its mixture weight. AMI is 44.65% versus 36.94% for mixed, and CHiME 6 is 77.41% versus 64.06%. VOiCES is similar at 17.91% versus 17.96%. The mixed recipe currently provides substantially stronger meeting robustness.

Quiet-view WER is 54.54%, better than the base 59.52% but worse than the mixed pilot 47.95%. All 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes produce zero inserted words. These probes do not establish performance with real background voices, very quiet product speech or the product microphone.

These short standalone pilots assess adaptation under a capped budget; they are not leave-one-dataset-out experiments and cannot isolate the marginal benefit of adding Common Voice to the mixture. Dataset exposure and audio duration differ despite the shared step cap. Scores are development evidence, not untouched final-test claims. No recipe promotion or weight change is due yet.

The supervisor has automatically started the AMI only pilot, which was advancing at step 1,770 of 10,000 at this check. CHiME 6 and VOiCES follow before the frozen weighting decision. The existing bounded campaign continues without extra trials or changes to its data policy.

entries.title: Interpretation of the completed AMI only pilot
paragraphs: The AMI only LoRA pilot completed 10,000 optimizer steps in 24.3 active training minutes, visiting 61,203 microphone views. Compilation, export and scoring are additional time. Best and final exports are byte-identical; their shared decode and timings are not independent measurements.

On the same 954-view development panel, macro WER is 31.85%, compared with 40.68% for the W4A8 base and 31.70% for the mixed pilot. The 8.83 percentage point gain over base is descriptive. Its 0.15-point deficit to mixed is too small to establish a meaningful ranking without the declared uncertainty analysis. The earlier full-duration initial final checkpoint remains at 28.06%, under a different training budget.

AMI WER improves to 34.78% versus 36.94% for mixed, and CHiME 6 is similar at 64.14% versus 64.06%. However, age-filtered Common Voice worsens to 9.04%, compared with 7.82% for mixed and 8.39% for base. VOiCES is also worse than mixed at 19.42% versus 17.96%, though still better than base at 20.64%. This illustrates a meeting-speech gain with a cost on older read voices; aggregate improvement alone does not justify choosing AMI only.

Quiet-view WER is 48.28%, similar to mixed at 47.95% and better than base at 59.52%. The 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes produce zero inserted words. Quiet-view error remains substantial, and these synthetic probes do not establish safety against invented words on real background voices or product-microphone recordings.

These are development results from capped standalone adaptation runs, not a causal estimate of removing or adding AMI within the mixture. Microphone views are related, and each pilot sees different audio duration and coverage. No weight or method decision has been saved yet. The supervisor automatically started CHiME 6, observed at step 1,330 of 10,000; VOiCES follows before the single permitted weighting proposal. No extra experiment or policy change is introduced.

entries.title: Interpretation of the completed CHiME 6 only pilot
paragraphs: The CHiME 6 only LoRA pilot completed 10,000 optimizer steps in 25.9 active training minutes, visiting 76,911 microphone views. Best and final exports are byte-identical, so their scoring and timings were reused. Compilation, export and scoring are additional to active training time.

On the unchanged 954-view development panel, macro WER is 36.24%, versus 40.68% for the W4A8 base and 31.70% for the mixed pilot. CHiME 6 itself improves substantially over base, from 85.38% to 65.96%, but remains worse than mixed at 64.06%. Every dataset has higher WER than the mixed pilot in this capped standalone experiment.

There are also regressions relative to base: age-filtered Common Voice WER rises from 8.39% to 9.83%, and VOiCES rises from 20.64% to 21.78%. AMI is 47.41%, only slightly better than base at 48.29% and substantially worse than mixed at 36.94%. The aggregate gain over base is therefore concentrated in CHiME 6, rather than consistent across settings.

Quiet-view WER is 58.71%, close to the base 59.52% and worse than mixed at 47.95%. All 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes still produce zero inserted words. This separates poor recognition of quiet speech from observed insertions on those specific synthetic probes; it does not establish behavior with real product microphones or background voices.

These development comparisons do not prove CHiME 6 should be removed from mixed training. Standalone adaptation is not a leave-one-dataset-out test, and the capped pilot covers only part of its expanded microphone-view pool. No weight or method decision is due yet. The supervisor automatically started the final individual-dataset pilot, VOiCES, observed at step 1,700 of 10,000. The frozen policy will then decide the single permitted weighting proposal; no extra trials or changes are introduced.

entries.title: VOiCES results and the single weighting proposal
paragraphs: The VOiCES only pilot completed 10,000 optimizer steps in 19.3 active training minutes, with 29,947 microphone-view visits across approximately 1.77 passes of its 16,929-view pool. Its best and final exports differ. Development scoring selected best at 40.19% macro WER, compared with 40.53% for final, 40.68% for the W4A8 base and 31.70% for the mixed pilot. The small aggregate gain over base does not establish a reliable general improvement.

VOiCES WER improves to 16.89%, compared with 20.64% for base and 17.96% for mixed. However, Common Voice worsens to 11.76%, versus 8.39% for base and 7.82% for mixed. AMI and CHiME 6 remain much worse than mixed at 46.94% and 85.15%. This is another example of narrow adaptation improving its own setting while sacrificing broader accuracy.

Best-checkpoint quiet-view WER is 58.53%, versus 59.52% for base and 47.95% for mixed. Both VOiCES exports produce zero inserted words on the 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes. This limited probe result does not offset the recognition regressions or establish behavior with real product microphones and background voices.

All four individual pilots are now complete. Macro development WER is 31.85% for AMI, 36.24% for CHiME 6, 36.93% for Common Voice and 40.19% for VOiCES; none beats mixed at 31.70%. These are standalone adaptation results, not causal marginal dataset contributions. Repeated microphone views and differing duration or coverage under the caps limit interpretation; frozen final tests are not used to select the recipe.

The supervisor followed the frozen proposal rule: AMI had the largest standalone macro gain over base, so its relative weight was multiplied by 1.5 and all four weights renormalized. The trial uses AMI 40.66%, Common Voice 34.65%, CHiME 6 16.04% and VOiCES 8.64%, versus prior AMI 31.36%, Common Voice 40.08%, CHiME 6 18.56% and VOiCES 10.00%. These are dataset loss-weight allocations, not dataset sizes or audio sampling percentages; the existing coverage and per-source microphone-confidence policies remain in place.

This weighting is a candidate, not an accepted production recipe. The weight_once pilot started automatically and was at 1,950 of 10,000 steps when checked. Its result must pass the declared development improvement, uncertainty, per-dataset and quiet/noise guards against mixed before promotion. Older-voice regressions in the standalone AMI run make that check especially relevant. The one full-tuning pilot follows under the frozen plan; no further weighting trials or policy changes are introduced.

entries.title: Weighting proposal rejected and full tuning pilot started
paragraphs: The single weighting pilot completed 10,000 steps in 36.7 active training minutes and visited 69,791 microphone views. Best and final exports are byte-identical, so their decoding and timings were reused. On the unchanged development panel, macro WER is 31.96%, compared with 31.70% for the original mixed reference.

The saved comparison measures a 0.26 percentage point increase in error, equivalent to a negative 0.82% relative gain. Its paired cluster 95% interval for candidate minus reference spans -0.31 to +0.84 percentage points, including zero. The candidate therefore fails the required improvement criterion and does not establish a reliable gain. This interval also does not prove a significant worsening, and it is not corrected for the entire model search.

All four dataset scores are descriptively worse under the proposed weighting: AMI 37.28% versus 36.94%, CHiME 6 64.43% versus 64.06%, Common Voice 7.96% versus 7.82%, and VOiCES 18.16% versus 17.96%. Quiet-view WER is 48.98% versus 47.95%, within the declared guard but not an improvement. Both models produce zero inserted words on the 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes. The quiet and silence/noise guards passed; lack of reliable accuracy improvement prevented promotion.

The supervisor rejected weight_once and retained mix_reference, using Common Voice 40.08%, AMI 31.36%, CHiME 6 18.56% and VOiCES 10.00% as dataset loss weights. This direct weighting experiment tests the proposed AMI increase more directly than standalone dataset pilots. It shows no benefit for that particular change under this budget, not that the retained weights are globally optimal or that AMI lacks value. No further weighting trial is added.

The final permitted method pilot, method_full, started automatically with the retained weights and learning rate 0.00001. Preflight completed, and full training was advancing at 960 of 10,000 steps at this check. No full-versus-LoRA decision is available yet. Its scoring and the frozen acceptance policy will determine the method for the single three-pass production fit; reporting does not hold that transition.

At the 24 October 2026 01:51 UTC snapshot, the dashboard planning range to the production model narrowed to approximately 27-54 hours remaining, from about 27-116 hours at the prior check. The upper bound changed because early measured full-tuning throughput replaced a broader estimate. The method remains undecided and these are planning estimates, not a firm deadline or statistical confidence interval; pauses, sleep and recovery can extend them. Development findings do not establish real product-microphone performance.

entries.title: LoRA selected for the final production fit
paragraphs: The full-tuning pilot completed 10,000 optimizer steps in 39.8 active training minutes, visiting 69,791 microphone views. Best and final exports are byte-identical and share their decode results. On the unchanged development panel, macro WER is 31.39%, slightly lower than the mixed LoRA reference at 31.70%. This is a 0.31 percentage point reduction and 0.98% relative improvement.

The saved policy rejected promotion to full tuning. The relative gain is below the required 2%, and the paired cluster 95% interval for candidate minus reference spans -2.13 to +1.90 percentage points, including zero. AMI also regresses by 2.011 percentage points, just above the declared two-point per-dataset limit. The evidence does not establish a sufficiently reliable, balanced improvement for this tested full-tuning recipe. It does not establish that full tuning can never help under other budgets or settings; no additional search is authorized in this bounded campaign.

Full tuning improves CHiME 6 WER to 61.21% from 64.06%, Common Voice to 7.68% from 7.82%, and VOiCES to 17.70% from 17.96%. AMI worsens to 38.95% from 36.94%. Quiet-view WER worsens to 50.18% from 47.95%, although it remains within the three-point guard. Both models produce zero inserted words on the 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes. Those probes do not validate behavior on real background voices or product microphones.

All seven permitted pilots and their development-based decisions are complete. The selected method is mixed LoRA with the original dataset loss weights: Common Voice 40.08%, AMI 31.36%, CHiME 6 18.56%, and VOiCES 10.00%. The production supervisor has automatically launched the single three-pass production_all_audio fit, using the full retained training and development pool with the existing microphone-alignment and quiet-channel safeguards. The final fit starts from the pretrained base under the selected recipe rather than continuing a pilot checkpoint.

At this check, production is in compilation and memory/gradient preflight, with 16 of 22 shapes complete and no production optimizer checkpoint yet. Its planned budget is 517,569 updates, with the declared larger LoRA batch limits of 16 examples, 120 padded audio seconds and 2,048 tokens. These are the existing production settings, not a new experiment. Monitoring remains at 15 minutes through startup; it can back off once production optimizer steps and checkpoints are advancing normally.

Development has now been folded into the final training pool after recipe selection, while frozen final tests remain excluded. The production model has not yet been evaluated, and development scores cannot serve as independent final accuracy evidence. There is no independent final age test or real product-microphone validation, and the screening has no second-seed confirmation. This is a bounded recipe choice, not proof of globally optimal weights or general superiority of LoRA.

At the 24 October 2026 02:36 UTC snapshot, the dashboard estimates approximately 26-45 hours remaining to a production model, including final export. This is a planning range based on the selected LoRA method and earlier throughput; it will be refined after production preflight and measured training progress. It excludes pauses, sleep and unexpected recovery time.

entries.title: First production fit completed and longer mixture comparisons started
paragraphs: The first production_all_audio fit completed all 517,569 optimizer updates and three passes through 2,413,566 retained training and development microphone views. Its final checkpoint records 7,240,698 view visits and 34.29 active training hours. These visits include repeated microphones of the same underlying speech and are not independent utterances. The completed LoRA model and export are preserved under the original production identity.

The periodic status file retains the last ten-step progress sample at step 517,560, but the final checkpoint confirms step 517,569, epoch 3 and next_batch 0. The run status reports that export is complete and comparison decoding is pending. This is a completed training and export milestone; it supplies no new measured accuracy gain or regression, quiet-speech score, or silence/noise result.

The supervisor has automatically begun ext_mix_reference from the pretrained base, using training data only and the original four-dataset relative weights. The declared ext_without_voices and ext_without_chime6 pilots follow. All three use the same qualified four-dataset development panel for evaluation. Each stops at 30,000 updates, two active hours or three passes, whichever comes first; compilation and scoring are additional.

The saved amendment requires at least 20,000 updates and 500 visited views per retained dataset in both reference and candidate before an omission can qualify, together with the original gain, uncertainty, dataset, quiet-speech and noise guards. The exposure minimum is an eligibility rule, not proof of statistical adequacy or a globally optimal mixture. Insufficient or inconclusive evidence keeps the completed production_all_audio model. Only a qualifying saved development decision can trigger the single additional three-pass production fit.

Development joined this first production fit after its original recipe selection, so its development performance would no longer be independent final evidence. The new comparisons retain their train-only separation by starting fresh from the pretrained base. Frozen production scoring remains deferred until the extension choice is fixed and will describe outcomes without choosing the recipe. Real product-microphone validation and an independent final age test remain unavailable.

entries.title: Longer mixed reference completed before the two omission comparisons
paragraphs: The longer mixed reference completed its 30,000-update cap in 109.2 active training minutes, within its two-hour limit. It visited 209,171 training microphone views: 128,115 CHiME 6, 70,078 AMI, 9,282 Common Voice and 1,696 VOiCES. These are view visits, not independent utterances. It meets the amendment's reference eligibility floor of 20,000 updates and 500 visited views per retained dataset. That floor does not prove convergence or statistical adequacy. Best and final exports are byte-identical and share one decode.

On the unchanged 954-view development panel, macro WER is 29.52%, compared with 31.70% for the 10,000-update mixed pilot: 2.18 percentage points lower, or 6.88% relative improvement. Base WER is 40.68%. The longer run improves all four dataset averages relative to the short pilot: AMI 33.71% versus 36.94%, CHiME 6 59.67% versus 64.06%, Common Voice 7.32% versus 7.82%, and VOiCES 17.36% versus 17.96%. These are descriptive differences; no paired uncertainty result for this duration comparison is saved. The earlier full-duration initial final model remains lower overall at 28.06%, under different duration and exposure.

The aggregate improvement does not mean every slice improved. The VOiCES clean slice rises from 4.57% to 5.08% WER, although its close and far slices improve. Quiet-view WER falls from 47.95% to 47.04%, but remains above the initial final model's 41.95%. All 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes produce zero inserted words. Quiet recognition errors remain substantial; the synthetic probe result does not establish behavior on real background voices or the product microphone.

The supervisor has automatically started ext_without_voices preflight; ext_without_chime6 follows. Both retain all four datasets in development evaluation. No omission is accepted or rejected yet. Each candidate must meet the declared exposure floor and the original gain, paired uncertainty, per-dataset and quiet/noise guards against this longer reference. An insufficient or inconclusive result retains the completed production_all_audio fit, with no additional trial.

This result demonstrates that the early capped mixed pilot left room for further measured improvement. It does not retrospectively make short standalone pilots sufficient for definitive dataset rankings or establish an optimal mixture. The new reference and omissions train only on training data from a fresh pretrained base. Production scoring remains deferred until recipe selection is fixed; the exported first production model is not evaluated by these pilot scores. Real product-microphone validation and an independent final age test remain unavailable.

entries.title: VOiCES omission does not improve the longer mixed reference
paragraphs: The VOiCES omission pilot completed its 30,000-update cap in 106.7 active training minutes, within the declared two-hour cap. It visited 211,414 training microphone views: 130,908 CHiME 6, 70,979 AMI and 9,527 Common Voice. Its completed run meets the amendment's 20,000-update and 500-view exposure floor for every retained dataset. The same 954-view, four-dataset development panel still includes VOiCES. View visits are not independent utterances, and the same step cap does not imply identical audio exposure.

Development scoring selected best at 30.34% macro WER, versus 30.40% for final. The exports are distinct and were decoded separately. The longer mixed reference is 29.52%, so the selected omission result is 0.82 percentage points worse, or 2.79% higher error. These point estimates do not meet the required improvement criterion. A paired uncertainty result and the combined extension decision have not yet been published; this descriptive difference does not establish statistically reliable worsening or a universal value for the dataset.

Relative to the longer mixed reference, AMI changes slightly from 33.71% to 33.64% WER and Common Voice is unchanged at 7.32%. CHiME 6 worsens from 59.67% to 60.86%. VOiCES worsens from 17.36% to 19.55%, a 2.19-point increase that also exceeds the declared two-point per-dataset guard. Its far-microphone slice rises from 33.97% to 38.46%. This experiment directly tests the declared omission recipe under a matched step cap; it supplies no evidence that removing VOiCES improves the mixture.

Quiet-view WER improves slightly from 47.04% to 46.82%. The selected model and the final export each produce zero inserted words on the 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes. Those limited probes do not validate real background voices or the product microphone. The small quiet-speech gain does not offset the required aggregate and per-dataset criteria.

The supervisor automatically started ext_without_chime6, the last planned extension pilot. No extension selection has been saved yet and no production refit is authorized by these results alone. The frozen policy will decide after all three longer pilots are complete; an insufficient or inconclusive outcome retains the preserved production_all_audio model. All these scores are development evidence from train-only pilots, not final production accuracy measurements. Frozen production scoring remains deferred until recipe selection, and real product-microphone validation and an independent final age test remain unavailable.

entries.title: Completed omission comparisons retain all four training datasets
paragraphs: The saved extension decision rejects both omissions and retains the mixed reference. Every longer pilot reached 30,000 updates and exceeded 500 visited views for every retained dataset, so these rejections are supported by measured results rather than insufficient exposure. The last pilot, without CHiME 6, completed in 82.9 active minutes and visited 181,394 microphone views: 156,873 AMI, 20,687 Common Voice and 3,834 VOiCES. Its development-selected best export scored 30.71% macro WER; its distinct final export scored 31.30%. Both identities remain recorded.

The longer mixed reference scored 29.52% development macro WER. Removing VOiCES raised error to 30.34%, a 0.82 percentage-point increase; the saved paired cluster 95% interval for candidate minus reference is +0.29 to +1.37 points. Removing CHiME 6 raised error to 30.71%, a 1.20-point increase, with interval +0.37 to +1.69 points. Both intervals lie above zero, supporting worsening within this declared comparison. Neither omission achieves the required 2% relative gain. These development intervals do not correct for the entire model search and do not establish a globally optimal mixture.

The CHiME omission improves AMI from 33.71% to 32.86% and VOiCES from 17.36% to 17.18%, but worsens Common Voice from 7.32% to 7.82% and CHiME 6 from 59.67% to 64.99%. The 5.32-point CHiME regression breaches the two-point per-dataset guard. The VOiCES omission also breaches that guard on VOiCES (+2.19 points). These tradeoffs show why the decision must include all four evaluation datasets, including the omitted training source.

Quiet-view WER is 47.04% for the mixed reference, 46.82% without VOiCES and 47.07% without CHiME 6. All selected exports have zero insertions on the 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes, and both omissions pass the saved quiet/noise guards. Passing those narrow guards does not compensate for aggregate and dataset regressions, or establish robustness on real product recordings.

The saved production decision requires no refit and preserves production_all_audio. Its all-audio LoRA recipe retains the original relative weights: Common Voice 0.4008074125, AMI 0.3135967650, CHiME 6 0.1855958224 and VOiCES 0.1. The campaign used 11 followup training runs: seven original pilots, the preserved production fit and three extension pilots; the one conditional twelfth run was not selected. Frozen production scoring followed recipe selection and did not choose or alter the recipe. No further trial is authorized by these results.

entries.title: Final campaign interpretation: AMI gain with broader regressions
paragraphs: The amended campaign and its matched frozen comparison are complete. The selected artifact remains the first production_all_audio fit, with no conditional refit. It completed three passes over 2,413,566 qualified train-plus-development microphone views: 7,240,698 visits and 517,569 updates in 34.29 active training hours. Repeated microphone views are not unique utterances. The exact first-production checkpoint identity and exported model are preserved; the longer reference pilot is evidence for retaining the recipe, not a replacement production model.

The frozen panel contains 512 clips, with 64 in each of eight cohorts. In the order base Whistle / initial tuned final export / final production / cached GigaSpeech, WER percentages are: AMI native 41.50 / 31.79 / 30.79 / 46.14; CHiME 6 native 71.45 / 63.23 / 66.43 / 71.73; CMU Arctic clean 12.59 / 12.06 / 12.59 / 5.77; HiFiTTS clean 3.41 / 3.96 / 4.84 / 1.76; HiFiTTS native 2.78 / 3.94 / 4.06 / 1.74; LibriSpeech clean 4.17 / 5.07 / 5.31 / 1.72; LibriSpeech native 11.73 / 13.81 / 14.26 / 6.14; VOiCES native 24.67 / 23.36 / 24.34 / 19.09. The generated comparison tables retain CER, runtime metrics and the distinct initial best export as well.

Relative to the initial tuned final export, production improves AMI by 0.99 percentage points but worsens the other seven cohorts, most visibly CHiME 6 by 3.20 points and VOiCES by 0.98 points. Relative to base Whistle it improves AMI, CHiME 6 and slightly VOiCES, ties CMU Arctic WER, and worsens both HiFiTTS and both LibriSpeech cohorts. Production beats cached GigaSpeech on AMI and CHiME 6 but trails it on the other six cohorts. These are measured domain tradeoffs; the final model is not a uniform accuracy improvement. No paired uncertainty interval for these frozen-test differences is supplied in the saved final summary, so small differences should not be presented as statistically established gains or losses.

The production model inserts zero words on the 20 fixed silence and Gaussian-noise probes. Its frozen-test quiet-audio summary contains zero marked clips and zero reference words, so it provides no final quiet-speech WER estimate. The development quiet results belong to the pilots and earlier models, not to an independent post-training age or quiet test of production. Energy thresholds reduce low-level contamination but do not guarantee intelligibility; the earlier audio audit quarantined near-silent speech and reserved CHiME annotations overlapping session seconds 0-1.

Its saved SHA256 is 96d9339d13eb8c16e677a9a737e5797a7f8d9999947d82289161a2c9539cec83 and its file size is 29,346,671 bytes. The initial tuned model remains at C:\Users\amiri\Documents\GitHub\just-peachy\training\whistle_age_robust_v1\whistle.final.cact; the initial best export remains alongside it. The original pretrained-base revision is 741118687e1f008f06d1351a402a731274789790. Cached GigaSpeech metrics are historical matched predictions, not a newly trained or remotely launched Giga model.

Retained training-data license provenance records Common Voice as CC0-1.0, AMI and VOiCES as CC-BY-4.0, and CHiME 6 as CC-BY-SA-4.0. CHiME 6 licensing was explicitly confirmed resolved by the user on 23 October 2026, with attribution records retained. The initial diagnostic checkpoints archived before the audio audit are distinct from the audited training and final production identities.

The final evidence does not include real product-microphone validation or an independent final age test, because development age data joined final training after recipe selection. Earlier limitations on the historical initial comparison, including VOiCES overlap, remain relevant. These bounded, single-seed comparisons do not establish an optimal mixture or broad deployment reliability. Production CPU timings were measured on the current Windows/WSL host; historical GigaSpeech latency is not directly comparable, and neither those timings nor the export size proves Raspberry Pi speed or memory suitability.

The next action is to preserve these models and findings and close the completed campaign; no additional training stage was selected. The report is published with its visual-layout limitation retained: no approved native renderer or connected Word session is available, and the earlier renderer setup was blocked by automatic approval review. Structural OOXML checks can establish package integrity but do not establish visual layout. This limitation does not prevent the completed training and analysis from being reported.

entries.title: Exploratory mixed transcription adaptation launched
paragraphs: The user authorized another training run on 25 October 2026, accepted exploratory evaluation while keeping the initial model as default, and allowed any dataset combination aimed at better transcription. The completed production campaign improved AMI but regressed against the initial final export in the other seven historical cohorts. That observation motivates this experiment; it does not establish that training on a single dataset would work better.

One new trajectory continues the preserved initial final adapter on its pinned original base, using a fresh optimizer. Its frozen schedule contains 100,000 visits to 80,513 distinct source utterances: 32,064 Common Voice visits, 25,088 AMI, 14,848 CHiME 6, 8,000 VOiCES and 20,000 clean LibriSpeech. The latter two contain 513 and 8,000 distinct source utterances respectively, so repeated visits must not be counted as independent speech. The four original domains reuse the completed quality audit, with clean replay added to practice retaining transcription of clean speech. This allocation is a bounded hypothesis, not an empirically optimal mixture.

The learning rate peaks at 0.00001 with 200 warmup updates; LoRA rank 16 and alpha 32 remain fixed. Training stops at the first of 10,000 updates, 3,600 actual optimizer-compute seconds or one pass through the frozen visit schedule. Loading, compilation, export and native scoring are additional time. At most five candidate validations apply the saved exposure, noisy-speech, age, clean-speech, quiet-speech and silence/noise guards, with declared early stopping. One candidate is frozen before exploratory confirmation. There is no extra trial, refit or automatic promotion; the initial model remains the default regardless of numerical results.

paragraphs: The separately authorized mixed-domain continuation finished at 4,000 optimizer updates after two consecutive validation checkpoints breached the saved retention limits. This result does not demonstrate a reliable broad transcription improvement, and it does not establish that single-dataset training would be better.

The run processed 20,225 example visits in 406.72 seconds of actual optimizer compute, approximately 6.78 minutes. It ended under the declared regression-based early-stop rule, before the maximum 10,000 updates, one-hour compute cap or full schedule pass. Actual visits were 6,433 Common Voice, 5,091 AMI, 2,985 CHiME 6, 1,703 VOiCES and 4,013 clean LibriSpeech. Distinct source counts were respectively 6,433, 5,091, 2,985, 502 and 3,408; repeated visits and microphone views are not independent utterances. On the identical frozen exploratory development panel, WER percentages in initial / 2,000-update / 4,000-update order are: AMI 26.82 / 26.67 / 27.66; CHiME 6 76.32 / 76.52 / 76.66; CMU Arctic clean 8.54 / 8.27 / 8.63; older-speaker Common Voice 12.29 / 12.21 / 11.80; HiFiTTS clean 7.48 / 7.79 / 7.56; HiFiTTS native 6.46 / 6.77 / 6.92; LibriSpeech clean 5.89 / 5.29 / 5.61; LibriSpeech native 10.27 / 10.22 / 10.49; VOiCES 12.51 / 11.84 / 12.02. Passing those negative probes does not establish accurate quiet-speech transcription, and energy screening is not an intelligibility guarantee.

These are development point estimates from one bounded trajectory. No paired confidence intervals or confirmation comparison were produced because no nonzero checkpoint passed development selection. VOiCES development contains only 26 source utterances and HiFiTTS clean only two speakers; the unused confirmation panel has one HiFiTTS clean speaker. entries.title: Complete full-parameter rerun launched on 26 October 2026
paragraphs: The user requested an entire rerun to seek incremental transcription improvement. One separately frozen trajectory starts from the same pinned pretrained base and trains all 55,151,433 parameters. The unchanged initial final model remains the default. This is an experiment, not evidence that full tuning improves accuracy.

All 2,052,751 qualified training views are retained: 220,174 distinct source utterances. Three passes schedule 6,158,253 view visits and 884,220 optimizer updates. Development intervals are not corrected for selecting among six checkpoints. No fresh independent confirmation, product-microphone validation or independent final age test is available.

GPU optimizer serialization and every batch shape are checked before actual training. There are no new accuracy results at launch. The Windows recovery monitor, existing heartbeat and CPU findings report are active for this new root. Prior models and completed policies remain preserved.

entries.title: Full rerun final selection and confirmation retain the initial model
paragraphs: The complete full-parameter QAT rerun finished all three passes, 884,220 updates and six native development validations. The frozen development decision selected step 442,110, then evaluated that candidate once on confirmation. Confirmation did not pass the numerical gates: CMU Arctic clean WER rose from 5.093% to 5.416%, a 0.323 percentage-point regression exceeding the 0.250-point clean-cohort retention limit. The complete nine-cohort confirmation interval is also undefined because HiFiTTS clean has only one reader. The saved decision retains the unchanged initial tuned model as default, with no promotion, runner-up selection, refit or additional trial.

The final checkpoint at step 884,220 achieved development macro WER 17.500% versus the initial tuned reference's 18.511%, an improvement of 1.010 percentage points. Its saved 95% macro delta interval is [-1.865, -0.174] points (checkpoint minus initial); all retention guards passed. Seven cohorts improved and the two LibriSpeech cohorts regressed. All nine individual cohort intervals include zero. This endpoint was 0.098 points worse on the development macro point estimate than the selected step 442,110; no checkpoint-to-checkpoint superiority interval was measured.

All 20 silence/noise probes remained empty (zero false-positive clips and zero inserted words).

The six development macro WERs in increasing checkpoint order were 18.066%, 17.805%, 17.402%, 17.684%, 17.639% and 17.500%. Step 147,370 failed CMU Arctic clean retention; the other five met the fixed development gain and retention rules. Selection used equal weighting of the nine cohorts and a minimum 0.200-point improvement, not the final checkpoint's position in the run. Step 442,110 improved development macro WER from 18.511% to 17.402% (1.108 points; saved 95% improvement interval 0.338 to 1.939 points). Six development cohorts improved; Common Voice age, HiFiTTS clean and LibriSpeech clean regressed within their guards.

AMI, CHiME-6 and VOiCES improved; CMU Arctic clean, HiFiTTS native and both LibriSpeech cohorts regressed; Common Voice age and HiFiTTS clean tied.
